Lena: Heads up — Prospect Nimbus (same account) asked for a slim POC to prove they can switch from VendorX with minimal client changes. Key asks: API surface compatibility, token billing alignment, and security questionnaire + KMS options. Can we scope?
Chris: We should prioritise a tiny adapter that accepts VendorX payloads and returns identical response shapes. Also a billing mapping doc from VendorX's 50-token-bucket billing to our per-token model.
Vik: I'll build the adapter. Plan: accept `X-VendorX-Session` and `VendorX-Model` headers, translate to Redwood fields, and optionally include `choices[].logprobs` if requested.
Aisha: Security: they want SOC2, IP allowlist, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and retention config. Also asking whether we can redact PII before logs hit S3.
Chris: For prompt parity, main deltas are tokenizer differences and sampling defaults. We'll run 6 templates with deterministic sampling (top_k=1 + seed) and compare tokenized inputs and outputs.
Lena: Nimbus wants a demo Thu. Can we have a runnable demo + cost estimate by Wed EOD?
Vik: Wed EOD doable for a prototype. Adapter example below:
```
POST /v1/vendorx/complete
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer <cust-token>",
  "X-VendorX-Session": "sess-77",
  "VendorX-Model": "vx-large-v2"
}
Body: {"input":"<text>", "max_tokens":100}
```
Adapter steps: 1) map `input` -> `prompt`, 2) lookup sess-77 -> fetch last 3 messages into KV, 3) call Redwood runtime with model mapping (vx-large-v2 -> rw-large-q4f), 4) transform Redwood response to VendorX shape including `choices[]`.
Aisha: Note: returning `logprobs` may surface token-level info customers consider sensitive. We should add a compatibility toggle in the adapter (logprobs on/off) and document perf tradeoffs.
Chris: Billing sim: VendorX lumps usage into 50-token buckets. Example: request using 31 tokens billed as 50. We'll run their sample logs through a script to compute Redwood-per-token costs and show delta. I'll attach a spreadsheet.
Vik: Compatibility mode will also support `choices[].finish_reason` and include `usage.total_tokens` field to help their billing UI.
Lena: Rate limits: VendorX enforces 120rpm with burst. Redwood hosted uses token throughput + concurrency caps. We'll propose a mapping: set concurrency=5 + token-rate limit approximated from their 120rpm bucket. Document fallback: if quota hit, return 429 with `retry_after` like VendorX.
Aisha: KMS: they want customer-managed KMS. Confirmed: Dedicated/Private supports CMK in customer's cloud. Hosted requires a dedicated workspace and additional paperwork. I'll draft the answers.
sec-bot: Reminder: Enabling CMK for hosted customers triggers SOC2 re-evaluation and needs approval from securityops. See internal runbook.
Chris: Action items: Vik -> adapter prototype + example curl (Wed AM). I -> run parity diffs on 6 prompts and produce short diff output. Aisha -> security Qs + KMS path + retention answers (Tue noon). Lena -> compile demo slide + cost delta.
Vik: Example curl for demo: 
```
curl -X POST https://demo.redwood/compat/vendorx \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer demo" \
  -H "X-VendorX-Session: sess-77" \
  -d '{"input":"List top three risks for Q3","max_tokens":60}'
```
Response will include `choices[0].text` and `usage.total_tokens` to match client parsing.
Chris: Parity caveat — tokenization differences can shift usage by +/- 2-8% depending on prompt. We'll show both raw diffs and a normalized cost estimate.
Aisha: Also include tradeoff doc: logprobs on = useful for downstream scoring but increases data sensitivity and CPU. Recommend default off; enable per-contract.
Lena: OK everyone — aim to drop artifacts here as you finish (adapter repo link, diff outputs, security Q doc, and pricing spreadsheet). Ping me when ready. :thumbsup:
